requirementSpec.intent: Build a polished Roblox main menu titled AURORA. Features: Play, Settings, Credits. Settings opens a panel with Music on/off toggle and Volume slider. Credits opens a small panel. Both panels have Close. Desktop and mobile. Rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details and a title plate. Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons: button skins, panel skin, slider track and handle, toggle on/off pieces and distinct play/settings/credits/close icons. Keep text live and readable. Create only these features; no shop, rewards, currency, ranks or invented game systems. Play closes the menu and fires a clearly named local hook for game integration. Coherent hover and press animation. Native background layout with restrained decoration. Panels must open and close in the actual controller.

designPlan.artDirection: A premium main menu built around a luminous cyan-to-cobalt gloss treatment framed by thick navy edging and restrained warm-gold accents. The composition avoids a full outer panel so the background stays native and calm, while the actionable menu cluster feels crafted and collectible. A single ornate title plate crowns the interface with live AURORA lettering, and sparing corner ornaments echo the same navy-and-gold detailing without clutter. Main buttons share one cohesive Gemini-generated skin family: Play is unmistakably dominant through scale and placement rather than a different unrelated hue, while Settings and Credits sit as aligned companion primary actions beneath it. The two modal panels reuse a single Gemini-generated glossy panel skin with readable live labels and compact internal structure. Slider and toggle controls receive matching illustrated control pieces so the settings surface feels complete and purpose-built. Overall mood is polished, glossy, heroic, and readable, with decoration supporting interaction rather than overwhelming it.

composition.focalPoint: The eye lands first on the AURORA title plate near upper center, then drops directly into the oversized Play button centered in the main dock. Settings and Credits continue the vertical reading order beneath Play. Secondary attention moves to the currently open modal panel, which overlays the dock without losing visual family continuity.

composition.alignmentSystem: Use a centered vertical axis for the title plate and main dock. Buttons align to a shared width and stack rhythm with even gaps. Modal panels also center on the same axis on desktop; on mobile they rise slightly upward to keep close and controls within thumb-safe reach. Decorative ornaments pin to screen corners and never compete with the central action stack.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt provide the requested rich glossy core, with navy supplying the thick structural edge language. Warm gold is reserved for highlights, title trim, and tiny emphasis lines so it reads premium rather than noisy. Background remains dark and restrained to preserve contrast for live text and to let the glossy surfaces carry the character of the screen.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Foreground surfaces use thick navy outer strokes with a slimmer inner gold or cyan highlight where artwork permits. Native text is not heavily outlined; instead readability comes from high contrast, careful placement, and subtle shadow separation on large headings only.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Use short, dense navy shadows under dock buttons and panels for weight, with a softer ambient shadow beneath the title plate. Shadows are layered and close to the object, supporting glossy depth without cartoon bounce.

display.treatment: Used only for AURORA. Wide tracking feel, crisp fill, subtle top highlight impression via surrounding plate art rather than text outline.

heading.treatment: Panel headings and major labels use clean bright text with restrained shadow for separation on glossy surfaces.

button.treatment: Centered live labels paired with icons. Strong contrast, no heavy outline, stable line height for readability over illustrated skins.

body.treatment: Readable utility text inside panels with generous spacing and high contrast against cobalt surfaces.

caption.treatment: Secondary supportive text such as credits body and small control descriptors.

numeric.treatment: Reserved for slider value readout if shown live in settings; compact but clear.

badge.treatment: Not emphasized in this screen; kept available for small state chips if needed by toggle internals.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Gemini-generated icon family with distinct play, settings, credits, and close symbols designed in the same premium cyan-cobalt-and-gold language as the skins. Shapes are clear at small sizes, front-facing, and slightly beveled through artwork rather than heavy 3D perspective.

motionSystem.hover: Pointer-capable devices use a restrained premium response: slight scale-up, subtle upward lift, and mild brightness or sheen increase. No exaggerated wobble. Modal surfaces remain stable while only actionable controls animate.
motionSystem.press: Buttons compress quickly with a short downward settle and clean rebound. Toggle and slider use compact state-responsive movement that feels tactile but not bouncy.
motionSystem.entrance: Initial menu entrance fades and rises in as one coordinated stack: title plate first, then main dock buttons, then hidden modals remain inactive until opened. Modal opening uses short scale-and-fade from 0.96 to 1.0 with overlay emphasis.
motionSystem.release: Controls return smoothly to resting scale with a slightly slower release than press for perceived polish. Modal close fades and shrinks minimally to maintain responsiveness.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, remove lift and scale amplification, keeping only quick opacity changes and instant state swaps for toggle and panel visibility.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only. No synthetic hover. Press feedback remains through scale compression and immediate state response.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds requested; touch relies entirely on visual feedback.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a future implementation adds sounds, unresolved assets must be reported and the interface must continue silently rather than pretending audio is present.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build a centered theatrical composition with the title plate occupying the upper third and a narrow button column beneath. Modal panels open in place over the menu, preserving the desktop's clean negative space and premium focus. Use the _NexusDesktop group visible initially.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build a separate _NexusMobile group rather than scaling desktop. Widen the button stack, increase button heights, reduce ornament intensity, and shift panels slightly upward for thumb-safe close and slider access. Keep Play dominant by size and order, not by introducing extra visual noise.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile structural group when viewport minimum dimension is below 600, otherwise favor a hybrid centered layout with desktop proportions softened toward larger touch targets. Keep panel widths between phone and desktop values and maintain the same action order.

implementationNotes: Use the supported library node names exactly: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsSeparator, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
View.build() must create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root frame groups with the same semantic node names beneath each; desktop visible initially.
Runtime selects mobile layout when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600; do not rely on Controller for initial structure existence.
MainMenuDock must remain transparent; do not add an outer menu panel or extra navigation features.
TitlePlate and BackgroundOrnaments each use one artwork slot with preserved aspect ratio.

PlayButton uses the primary button skin; SettingsButton and CreditsButton share one identical secondary skin; SettingsCloseButton and CreditsCloseButton share one compact close skin and one close icon family treatment.
SettingsModal and CreditsModal share one panel skin artwork family, with CreditsModal sized smaller by layout only.

MusicToggle and VolumeSlider should use control_artwork treatments so downstream resolver can provide matching slider track, slider handle, and toggle on/off pieces without adding separate planned components.
Keep all requested labels live text. Do not rasterize AURORA, button labels, settings labels, or credits copy into images.
PanelControllerBehavior should open settings on open_settings_panel, open credits on open_credits_panel, close the respective panel on close actions, and ensure only one modal is visible at a time.
PlayButton activation should first hide the menu via close_menu behavior, then fire the clearly named local hook on OnPlayRequestedHook for integration.
Implement hover only for pointer-capable devices; touch uses Activated and press feedback only.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated styling and layout creation. Put runtime button animation behavior in a shared ButtonEffects module rather than per-button copies.

Use UIListLayout and UIPadding for all stacks; use UITextSizeConstraint on live text; use UIAspectRatioConstraint for title plate and ornaments; use UIScale for responsive visual tuning; use UIStroke and UICorner where native framing complements the artwork.
Do not add shop, rewards, currency, ranks, inventory, quests, tabs, or any invented system components.
Credits body should remain concise generic live text unless project-specific credits are later injected; keep the panel small as requested.
Audio is intentionally silent because sounds were not requested; unresolved audio must not be fabricated.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Gemini-generated icon family with distinct play, settings, credits, and close symbols designed in the same premium cyan-cobalt-and-gold language as the skins. Shapes are clear at small sizes, front-facing, and slightly beveled through artwork rather than heavy 3D perspective.

motionSystem.hover: Pointer-capable devices use a restrained premium response: slight scale-up, subtle upward lift, and mild brightness or sheen increase. No exaggerated wobble. Modal surfaces remain stable while only actionable controls animate.
motionSystem.press: Buttons compress quickly with a short downward settle and clean rebound. Toggle and slider use compact state-responsive movement that feels tactile but not bouncy.
motionSystem.entrance: Initial menu entrance fades and rises in as one coordinated stack: title plate first, then main dock buttons, then hidden modals remain inactive until opened. Modal opening uses short scale-and-fade from 0.96 to 1.0 with overlay emphasis.
motionSystem.release: Controls return smoothly to resting scale with a slightly slower release than press for perceived polish. Modal close fades and shrinks minimally to maintain responsiveness.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, remove lift and scale amplification, keeping only quick opacity changes and instant state swaps for toggle and panel visibility.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only. No synthetic hover. Press feedback remains through scale compression and immediate state response.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds requested; touch relies entirely on visual feedback.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a future implementation adds sounds, unresolved assets must be reported and the interface must continue silently rather than pretending audio is present.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build a centered theatrical composition with the title plate occupying the upper third and a narrow button column beneath. Modal panels open in place over the menu, preserving the desktop's clean negative space and premium focus. Use the _NexusDesktop group visible initially.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build a separate _NexusMobile group rather than scaling desktop. Widen the button stack, increase button heights, reduce ornament intensity, and shift panels slightly upward for thumb-safe close and slider access. Keep Play dominant by size and order, not by introducing extra visual noise.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile structural group when viewport minimum dimension is below 600, otherwise favor a hybrid centered layout with desktop proportions softened toward larger touch targets. Keep panel widths between phone and desktop values and maintain the same action order.

implementationNotes: Use the supported library node names exactly: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsSeparator, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
View.build() must create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root frame groups with the same semantic node names beneath each; desktop visible initially.
Runtime selects mobile layout when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600; do not rely on Controller for initial structure existence.
MainMenuDock must remain transparent; do not add an outer menu panel or extra navigation features.
TitlePlate and BackgroundOrnaments each use one artwork slot with preserved aspect ratio.

PlayButton uses the primary button skin; SettingsButton and CreditsButton share one identical secondary skin; SettingsCloseButton and CreditsCloseButton share one compact close skin and one close icon family treatment.
SettingsModal and CreditsModal share one panel skin artwork family, with CreditsModal sized smaller by layout only.

MusicToggle and VolumeSlider should use control_artwork treatments so downstream resolver can provide matching slider track, slider handle, and toggle on/off pieces without adding separate planned components.
Keep all requested labels live text. Do not rasterize AURORA, button labels, settings labels, or credits copy into images.
PanelControllerBehavior should open settings on open_settings_panel, open credits on open_credits_panel, close the respective panel on close actions, and ensure only one modal is visible at a time.
PlayButton activation should first hide the menu via close_menu behavior, then fire the clearly named local hook on OnPlayRequestedHook for integration.
Implement hover only for pointer-capable devices; touch uses Activated and press feedback only.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated styling and layout creation. Put runtime button animation behavior in a shared ButtonEffects module rather than per-button copies.

Use UIListLayout and UIPadding for all stacks; use UITextSizeConstraint on live text; use UIAspectRatioConstraint for title plate and ornaments; use UIScale for responsive visual tuning; use UIStroke and UICorner where native framing complements the artwork.
Do not add shop, rewards, currency, ranks, inventory, quests, tabs, or any invented system components.
Credits body should remain concise generic live text unless project-specific credits are later injected; keep the panel small as requested.
Audio is intentionally silent because sounds were not requested; unresolved audio must not be fabricated.

changeInstructions: Create a polished main menu titled AURORA.
Include Play, Settings, and Credits as the only main menu features.
Make Settings open a panel containing a Music on/off toggle and a Volume slider.
Make Credits open a small panel.
Provide Close controls for both panels.
Make Play close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration.
Use rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate.
Use Gemini-generated matching skins and distinct icons for specified components.
Apply coherent hover and press animation.
Implement panel open/close behavior in the actual controller.
Use a native background layout with restrained decoration.
Support desktop and mobile.
preserve: Do not add shop, rewards, currency, ranks, or invented game systems.
Limit product structure to the explicitly requested main menu and its two panels.
